newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals prices steady on LME trends.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals prices steady on LME trends.

text.p: Prices of most Indian metals were steady during the week, in line with the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said on Wednesday.
They said customs duty changes on aluminium and other basic products in the 1997/98 (April-March) federal budget presented last month would not have an immediate impact on the market.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in his budget halved import duty on nickel to 10 percent to help the domestic steel industry, in which nickel is a crucial component.

Chidambaram reduced import duty on tin to 20 percent from 30 percent to help the domestic alloys industry and provided relief to the aluminium industry, by raising import duty on aluminium by 10 percent to 20 percent.
Industry officials said India had sufficient stocks of aluminium.
The domestic aluminium industry is saddled with inventories and the duty changes were aimed at giving relief to them.
"The duty increase will not affect the market right now," Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metals Exchange, told Reuters.
"Traders will not immediately go for imports. There are sufficient stocks and users will procure from state firms," Parikh said.
India annually imports about 60,000 tonnes of the metal.
The country has an annual production capacity of 610,000 tonnes of aluminium metal but output is much lower. It annually consumes around 500,000 tonnes of metal.
The budget also reduced import duty on concentrates of copper and zinc to 5.0 percent from 10 percent to help domestic producers importing raw materials.
Mines Ministry officials said the cut in customs duty on copper concentrates would have a positive impact on the profitability of state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd and help its expansion plans.
HCL had asked the government to increase import duties on the metal to overcome a cash crunch.

In the week up to Wednesday, copper, aluminium, lead and tin prices remained unchanged from last week, zinc fell by 250 rupees per tonne while nickel gained 3,000 rupees. Import prices for aluminium ingots were 63.35 rupees per kg at Indian ports.
